 CORAM:
 JUSTICE G. SATAPATHY  ORDER Order No. 21.04.2023  01. 1. This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. This is an application U/S. 439 of Cr.P.C. by the Petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Charmal P.S. Case No. 164 of 2022 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 65 of 2022 pending in the file of learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Sambalpur for commission of offence punishable U/Ss. 363/376(2)(n) of IPC, r/w Section-6 of the POCSO Act, on the allegation of kidnapping the victim and committing rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.
3. In the course of hearing of the bail application, Mr. S. Bahadur, learned counsel for the Petitioner by placing the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim // 2 // submits that there is absolutely no material against the Petitioner for commission of any offence and the Petitioner having already been unnecessarily harassed by remaining custody since 02.12.2022 and in the meanwhile, charge-sheet having been submitted in this case, it is, accordingly, prayed by learned counsel to grant bail to the Petitioner.
4.

1 of the Petitioner by inter-alia contending that the statement of the victim recorded U/S. 161 Cr.P.C.
discloses a strong prima facie case against the Petitioner for kidnapping the victim and committing aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her and, thereby, the Petitioner is not entitled to bail.

5. After considering the rival submissions made and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of accusations raised against the Petitioner and keeping in view the manner and circumstance of the allegation against the Petitioner and regard being had to the pre- trial detention of the Petitioner since 02.12.2022 and taking into account the submission of charge-sheet in this case and on going through the statement of the victim recorded U/S. 164 Cr.P.C., this Court admits the Petitioner to bail.
6.

Hence, the bail application of the Petitioner stands allowed and the Petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees // 3 // Twenty Five Thousand) with two solvent sureties for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the Petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail (ii) the Petitioner shall attend the trial Court on each date of posting without fail unless his attendance is dispensed with (iii) the Petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till disposal of the case

It is clarified that the Court in seisin of the case is at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioner without further reference to this Court, if any of the above conditions are violated or a case for cancellation of bail is otherwise made out.

In the wake of aforesaid, the subsequent involvement of the petitioner in future for grave and serious offences on prima facie accusations may be treated as a ground for cancellation of bail in this case.
7. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
8. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.

( G. Satapathy) Judge Priyajit // 4 //
